title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). M is a 'magasin', a store of elementary figures or strata, carrying relations ≤, ≪, a compatibility/incompatibility relation and |o|. F_M is the set of M-figures, i.e. admissible subsets of M. An M-situation 𝓕 is an 'antifiltre' in F_M: it is downward closed for ≤, closed under existing binary sups F∨G, and contains the elementary figures X̃ (X∈M) and the empty figure.

This page.
(1) The relations ≤, ≪, ≭, ∥ on F_M restrict to 𝓕. Propositions 1∘F, 2∘F (p. 2 bis) and Props 2, 3, 5 then hold 'ipso facto' when one works in a general atlas.
(2) Only Prop. 4, the gluing ('recollement') of refinements, needs an extra stability axiom when the index set I is infinite. This is axiom At Fil. Let F∈𝓕 and let (G_α) be a family of refinements of F, filtered increasing for ≤. Suppose that for every elementary X≤F the restricted family G_α|X is eventually stationary. Then Sup G_α exists in 𝓕. When 𝓕⊂F_M, this says the union ∪G_α, which is the sup in F_M, already lies in 𝓕. So 𝓕 is closed under 'locally stationary' directed unions of refinements, a closedness condition on 𝓕 inside (F_M, ≤).
(3) Change of viewpoint: from a set of figures built on a given M to an intrinsic structure. An 'atlas' is a poset 𝓕 with three relations ≤, ≪, |o|, subject to:
- At 1: bounded ('majorés') sups exist, and 𝓕≠∅. Together these are equivalent to 𝓕 having a least element φ, the sup of the empty family. So 𝓕 is a bounded-complete poset.
- Elementary figures (strata) are defined as the completely join-irreducible elements: X = Sup F_i ⇒ ∃i, F_i = X. M is the set of these, and F̃ = {X∈M | X≤F}.
- At 2: F≤G ⇔ F̃⊂G̃ ('every stratum of F is a stratum of G'). Equivalently, every figure is the Sup of its strata, i.e. M join-generates 𝓕.

Next page. Compatibility is defined as 'F∨G exists'. At 3 says compatibility is checked stratum-by-stratum (pairwise, binary coherence). At 4 reduces ≪ to strata. At 5 puts |o| on M. A Scholie states that the 'magasin' presentation (M with relations, 𝓕⊂F_M, axioms Mag 1–4) and the 'atlas' presentation (𝓕 with At 1–5 + Mag 1–4) give equivalent groupoids.

Modern reading: this is a Stone-type representation theorem. A bounded-complete poset that is join-generated by complete primes, with binary coherence, is recovered as the down-closed, pairwise-compatible subsets of its primes. The primes carry an order (frontier/closure of strata) and a conflict relation.
errors: No mathematical error detected. Under At 1, F̃ is bounded by F, so Sup F̃ exists and is ≤F. Hence At 2 ⇔ 'F = Sup F̃' is correct.
The irreducibility definition implicitly excludes the empty family, so φ is not elementary. That is consistent, but it is not stated.

At Fil is stated somewhat informally. 'Refinement' and the restriction G_α|X are defined on earlier pages not shown here, and the conclusion line (whether Sup G_α is again a refinement of F) is crossed out and left incomplete.

ideas.what: Axiom At Fil: existence of sups of filtered families of refinements that are locally stationary on each stratum (closure of 𝓕 under such directed unions); needed only for infinite gluing of refinements
ideas.modern_name: restricted directed-completeness / local finiteness condition (cf. directed-complete subsets, locally finite refinement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in domain theory (Scott) in general form

ideas.what: Atlas viewpoint: bounded-complete poset with least element, elementary figures = completely join-irreducibles, every figure = Sup of its strata
ideas.modern_name: prime-algebraic bounded-complete (coherent) poset; join-generation by complete primes

ideas.what: Equivalence between the 'magasin' presentation (elementary strata with order and incompatibility; figures as admissible subsets) and the intrinsic 'atlas' presentation (next page's Scholie)
ideas.modern_name: representation duality: event structures ↔ prime algebraic coherent domains; webs ↔ coherence spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck, aiming at a combinatorial foundation of 'analysis situs' (figures made of strata, ordered by frontier/closure), independently arrives at the duality between prime-algebraic bounded-complete posets and their 'webs' of primes with order and incompatibility. This is the same structure as event structures/configurations (Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981) and coherence spaces (Girard 1986–87). The link between stratified/tame geometry (figures as configurations of strata) and the domain-theoretic event-structure duality does not seem to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: On peut considérer la structure d'atlas comme une donnée indépendamment de celle d'un magasin ... Atlas : 𝓕 muni de trois relations ≤, ≪, |o| ... Figures élémentaires ... irréductibles: X = Sup F_i ⇒ ∃i, F_i = X ... Toute figure est le Sup de ses strates
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could supply a domain-theoretic or order-theoretic semantics for combinatorial stratified spaces (face posets, regular CW complexes, tame-topology 'figures'), including refinements. It might also offer a geometric reading of event structures and concurrency models (cf. directed topology).

missed.claim: The axiom At Fil, ensuring that infinite gluing of refinements (Prop. 4) works, is formulated but its conclusion is crossed out and incomplete. Whether the sup is again a refinement of F is left open.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the minimal completeness condition for infinite subdivision or refinement in an axiomatic tame-topology framework, but it was not settled here.

deep.surprise_reason: The order theory itself is a rediscovery of known domain-theory and event-structure dualities, though this was contemporaneous with Girard and independent. The mildly notable point is the geometric motivation, strata of figures in an axiomatic 'analysis situs', and the explicit magasin/atlas equivalence, which seems absent from the literature.
